catalog_quote: Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) In verbs the stress falls on the first /ɑ/ or first syllable of singular person number of the present and past tenses. In the future tense and dual and plural person number of the present and past tenses the stress falls on the final syllable. In all other words, the stress falls on the first /ɑ/ or diphthong or first syllable if there is none of these. ... Conventions: Phonological The vowel [ɑ] is pronounced [ʌ] in unstressed syllables.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both quoted passages are verbatim on the OPD page scan we hold (p.3 Suprasegmentals; p.4 Conventions: Phonological). (2) Deciding source: a 5-page SIL OPD summary (Stucky data 1994) whose sole bibliography entry is Stucky 1990 mss. I located and downloaded the parent, Stucky & Stucky 1990 'Melpa Phonology' (44-pp. scan, SIL PNG item 52243, via the Internet Archive of www-01.sil.org), which is Glottolog's principal modern phonology for Melpa; its section 8 (pp.34-35) states the same rules almost word for word ('In all other words, the stress falls on the 1st /a/ or dipthongs or 1st syllable in that preferential order'), so the catalog's classification (classification segmental: leftmost /a/-or-diphthong syllable, else initial, unbounded; verb stress set by tense/number) is confirmed by the best available source.
